碎音鈸具有明亮刺激的音色質感，能夠產生尖銳而富有穿透力的音響效果。其音域位於高頻: The crash cymbal has a bright, exciting sound and can produce a sharp, penetrating effect. It sits in the high frequency range and is rich in overtones, which gives it a strong metallic sheen. Its resonance is quick and direct: after the strike the sound peaks at once and then decays fast. Where the ride cymbal is low and round, the crash is sharper and more exciting; beside the complex blur of clashing cymbals, its sound is clearer and more focused. It feels cool rather than warm, with strong impact and dramatic tension, which makes it particularly good for marking accents and building the high point of a piece. In rock, jazz or classical line-ups alike, the crash cymbal's particular metallic quality and high-frequency penetration make it an indispensable colour in the band.
碎音鈸可裝在支架上以鼓棒敲擊，也可雙手各持一片互擊；管弦樂撞擊鈸以皮帶穿過中心孔: A crash cymbal can be mounted on a stand and struck with a drumstick, or one can be held in each hand and clashed together; in the orchestra clash cymbals are held by a strap threaded through the centre hole. When mounted, it can be struck with a single stick or rolled with a pair of mallets for a slower, swelling crash. A beginner first strikes at a slant rather than square on, hitting about a quarter of the way between the edge and the centre so that the stick bounces off naturally, and avoiding a flat, pressed hit. A right-handed drummer traditionally puts the crash on the left of the kit, though it can also be set on the right or in multiples as needed.

In the kit it is mostly used for occasional accents rather than a steady rhythm pattern; in rock, drummers sometimes strike two different crashes at once for a very loud accent. A mounted crash can be struck with a stick or rolled repeatedly with a pair of mallets for a slower, looser wash. The pair of clash cymbals is standard orchestral percussion, and also appears on stage, in concerts and in military bands.

The crash cymbal is an unpitched idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.24, in the cymbal family of the Europe | regional / culture area. It can be mounted on a stand and struck with drumsticks, or clashed in pairs by hand; a drum kit usually carries one or two, and bands, orchestras, marching bands and military bands use them too. Its main job is to produce a sharp, loud accent; a mounted one can be rolled with a stick or a pair of mallets so that the sound swells more slowly; striking two different crashes at once can produce a stronger accent, which is common in rock music.
碎音鈸由青銅合金（通常為銅錫合金）製成，含銅80%、錫20%左右。鈸面採用精選的: A crash cymbal is made of bronze alloy, usually copper and tin, at roughly 80 % copper and 20 % tin. The cymbal is cut from selected bronze sheet, cast precisely and shaped by hand hammering. The edge is carefully ground so that it sounds clear. The surface is usually polished or given a bronze finish. The mount uses a steel bolt and a pad, the pad usually of rubber or cork, to reduce loss of vibration and let the cymbal ring freely.
碎音鈸起源於中國古代，早期作為宗教儀式和軍事用途的樂器。其構造理念隨著絲綢之路傳: Cymbals go back to ancient China, where they were at first instruments of religious ritual and military use. The idea of their construction travelled the Silk Road to the Middle East and Europe, gradually becoming the modern form. In the nineteenth century European makers began industrial production of cymbals and improved the design. The crash cymbal developed greatly with the rise of jazz and became essential to the jazz drum kit, drummers using its sharp sound to mark the strong beats. In the mid-twentieth century the spread of rock pushed playing further, and drummers began striking two cymbals at once for a stronger effect. Today the crash cymbal is a core part of modern percussion, widely used in jazz, rock, classical music and other styles, and its manufacture has kept improving with the times.
